title: Fattoush
subtitle: Lebanese bread salad with sumac dressing
excerpt: A bright Lebanese salad of crisp toasted pitta, fresh cucumber, tomato, radish, and herbs dressed with tangy sumac vinaigrette. Crunchy, fresh, and sharp.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fattoush is a Lebanese bread salad (the name comes from the Arabic fatteh, meaning crumbled bread) that uses stale or toasted pitta as the carbohydrate base. It is one of the oldest categories of bread salad in the Levantine kitchen, related to the Italian panzanella in concept though very different in flavour. The defining ingredient is sumac: a tart, berry-like spice ground from the dried berries of the sumac shrub, which provides the characteristic citrusy sharpness. The pitta is toasted or fried until crisp before being added to the salad, and it should retain some crunch at the point of serving rather than becoming soggy. The salad is assembled and dressed immediately before serving. The vegetables are seasonal: purslane, if available, is the most traditional addition in Lebanese versions but cucumber and radish are the most commonly available substitutes.

content.text: Toast the pitta in the oven until completely crisp and golden before breaking into shards: the pitta must be very dry or it will become soggy in the dressing within minutes. The salad should be assembled and dressed just before eating. The sumac provides most of the acidity: taste the dressing before adding the lemon juice as sumac varies in strength between brands.

items.preparation: torn into shards and toasted until crisp

content.text: Tear the pitta into rough shards. Toast in a 200 C oven for 8 to 10 minutes until completely golden and crisp. Set aside to cool.
Whisk together the sumac, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, radish, spring onion, parsley, and mint in a large bowl. Add the toasted pitta. Pour over the dressing and toss gently. Serve immediately.
